sasha: Heads-up — multi-node TP job keeps hanging during rendezvous when we scale to 16 nodes. Seen twice today on staging-3 and staging-7.

mike: Which commit/branch? any recent kernel selector or batching changes rolled?

sasha: Running main @ a2f9c3. We rolled batching heuristics change (PR#3421) and kernel-selector tweak (PR#3390) last night.

julia: Logs? stack traces?

sasha: Pasting stripped logs:
```
[rank0] wait_for_rendezvous timeout after 120s
[rank0] last op: allreduce(size=1.2GB) gid=42
[rank5] reduced bytes mismatch: expected 1.2GB got 1.1GB -> stall
[rank*] kv_cache hit ratio ~85% when it stalls
```

kevin: Interesting — allreduce sizes are large. Could be per-rank buffer size skew. Any changes to kv cache padding or TP partitioning?

sasha: We changed kv cache padding to align to 4096 bytes recently (was 1024). The theory is padding increased tensor sizes on some ranks.

mike: Can you repro with lower scale and run nvprof / tracemalloc? Also check nccl timeouts (NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING).

sasha: Repro command I used: `./run_inference --model gpt-xl --tp 16 --nodes 4 --batch 8 --seed 42 --profile`.

julia: I captured a perf profile on one run. Attaching flame snippet (trimmed):
```
timeline: compute (60%) | waiting-allreduce (30%) | kv-serialize (10%)
ranks 0,1,2 show waiting spike at step ~42
```

kevin: Could be comm/compute imbalance — maybe kernel selector chose a slower kernel for certain tensor shapes after padding. That would delay allreduce posting and cause other ranks to block.

mike: Check kernel selection logs (we log chosen kernel id per op). Also compare tensor shapes across ranks: `env DEBUG_KSEL=1 ./run_inference ...`

sasha: Ran with DEBUG_KSEL. Rank 0 picked kernel `matmul_v2_opt` for shapes [2048, 3072], rank 5 picked `matmul_v1` for apparently identical shapes but different padding.

julia: So same logical shape but different physical stride due to kv padding -> different kernel; performance asymmetry.

kevin: That explains queuing. But why does it lead to allreduce size mismatch that blocks? NCCL expects all ranks to post the same byte count for the op. If padding changes buffer bytes, some ranks post smaller byte counts causing mismatch until they match.

mike: Another angle: batching heuristics may be merging sequences differently per rank when kv cache hits vary, causing transient batch size divergence. Combine that with padding change -> different allreduce sizes.

sasha: I reproduced a minimal repro by toggling kv padding:
- padding=1024 -> no hang
- padding=4096 -> hang at ~step 42

julia: Good repro. Any quick mitigation? We can revert padding or force kernel selection to a consistent codepath (e.g., override to `matmul_v2_opt`) as a hotfix.

kevin: Also consider aligning allreduce to logical size not physical buffer. There's an existing NCCL wrapper that uses `tensor.numel()`; but if buffers are padded we must use the padded size consistently across ranks.

mike: For emergency: Revert PR#3419 that bumped padding, or set runtime flag `REDWOOD_KV_PAD=1024` for Dedicated staging pools.

sasha: Rolling a patch to staging with `REDWOOD_KV_PAD=1024` now. Will monitor. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

infra-bot: deploy-job staging/kv-pad-hotfix started (job id: dj-8801).

sasha: After hotfix run: no hangs for ~2 hours at scale 16. Early success.

julia: Root cause summary suggestion: padding change increased physical buffer stride causing kernel-selector divergence + batching variance led to per-rank allreduce byte mismatch -> NCCL rendezvous timeout.

kevin: Agreed. Action items: 1) revert kv padding change or add compatibility layer; 2) add unit test verifying per-rank buffer sizes for allreduce ops; 3) add CI profiling job that runs scaled TP smoke with debug flags; 4) PR to kernel-selector to prefer stable kernel across padding variants when latency difference < 5%.

mike: Logging/observability: add metric `allreduce_post_bytes` per-rank and an alert if SD across ranks > 1% for same op id.

sasha: I'll open PRs: revert/patch for padding (PR 3460), kernel-selector adjustment (PR 3461), alerting (PR 3462).

julia: Nice triage. Can you paste exact repro logs for the postmortem? Keep them short.

sasha: Copying key excerpt for PM:
```
step 42: rank0 chosen kernel matmul_v2_opt, post bytes 1.228GB
step 42: rank5 chosen kernel matmul_v1, post bytes 1.096GB
NCCL: expected 1.228GB from peer ranks, got smaller -> timeout
kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.85
kv_pad=4096
```

kevin: Perfect. I'll add to incident notes and link PRs. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
